heading: Benefits and Wellbeing > Health insurance
text:
Benefits and Wellbeing > Health insurance
All permanent employees are covered by private health insurance through **Corvane Health**, starting on day one. Partners and children can be added at no extra cost. Dental is included; optical care is covered up to €250 per year.

heading: Benefits and Wellbeing > Pension
text:
Benefits and Wellbeing > Pension
Brindlewick matches your pension contributions up to 6% of your base salary. Enrolment is automatic after your first month; you can opt out in Peoplepath.

heading: Benefits and Wellbeing > Learning budget
text:
Benefits and Wellbeing > Learning budget
Each employee has a learning budget of €1,500 per calendar year for courses, conferences, books and certifications. You also get 5 learning days per year that do not count as annual leave. Unused budget does not roll over.

heading: Benefits and Wellbeing > Wellbeing allowance
text:
Benefits and Wellbeing > Wellbeing allowance
You receive €60 per month to spend on anything that supports your wellbeing: gym membership, sports clubs, therapy, meditation apps or massage. Claim it through Ledgerline.

heading: Benefits and Wellbeing > Bike leasing
text:
Benefits and Wellbeing > Bike leasing
Employees can lease a bike or e-bike through the company bike scheme. The cost is deducted from your gross salary over 36 months, which saves tax.

heading: Benefits and Wellbeing > Employee assistance programme
text:
Benefits and Wellbeing > Employee assistance programme
A free, confidential counselling service is available 24/7 to employees and their families. Up to 8 sessions per year are covered. The phone number is in Peoplepath under "Wellbeing".

heading: Code of Conduct > Respect at work
text:
Code of Conduct > Respect at work
Brindlewick does not tolerate harassment, discrimination or bullying of any kind, whether in the office, at the factory, at company events or online. This applies to how we treat colleagues, customers, suppliers and visitors.

heading: Code of Conduct > Gifts and hospitality
text:
Code of Conduct > Gifts and hospitality
You may accept gifts from customers or suppliers worth up to €50. Gifts worth more than €50 must be declined or declared to your manager, who decides whether you may keep them. Cash or cash-equivalent gifts (such as vouchers) are never allowed.

heading: Code of Conduct > Conflicts of interest
text:
Code of Conduct > Conflicts of interest
Declare any situation where your personal interests could conflict with Brindlewick's — for example, a family member working for a supplier, or a side business in robotics. Declare it in Peoplepath under "Declarations". Side jobs are allowed if they do not compete with Brindlewick and you declare them.

heading: Code of Conduct > Speaking up
text:
Code of Conduct > Speaking up
If you see behaviour that breaks this code, report it. You can:

1. Talk to your manager or the People Team.
2. Use **Speak Up**, the anonymous ethics line, available in Peoplepath.

The Conduct Committee acknowledges every report within 2 business days and gives an initial response within 10 business days.

heading: Code of Conduct > No retaliation
text:
Code of Conduct > No retaliation
Nobody will be punished for raising a concern in good faith, even if the concern turns out to be unfounded. Retaliation against someone who reported a concern is itself a serious breach of this code.

heading: Brindlewick Robotics — Company Overview > Who we are
text:
Brindlewick Robotics — Company Overview > Who we are
Brindlewick Robotics designs autonomous sorting robots for small and mid-sized warehouses. Our flagship product, the Sorter-9, can handle up to 1,200 parcels per hour and is used by more than 180 customers across Europe.

The company was founded in 2017 in Port Halden by Marisol Ekwueme (CEO) and Tobias Rennick (CTO). As of this handbook's latest revision, Brindlewick employs 340 people.

heading: Brindlewick Robotics — Company Overview > Offices
text:
Brindlewick Robotics — Company Overview > Offices
- **Port Halden (HQ):** Engineering, product, finance and people operations. Located at 14 Quayside Lane.
- **Kettering Bay:** Manufacturing, hardware testing and field support.
- **Remote:** About 30% of employees work fully remotely from approved countries.

heading: Brindlewick Robotics — Company Overview > Our values
text:
Brindlewick Robotics — Company Overview > Our values
1. **Build it to last.** We design for ten-year hardware lifetimes, not product launches.
2. **Say the hard thing early.** Raise risks the day you see them, not the day before a deadline.
3. **Leave the warehouse better.** Every feature must make a warehouse worker's day safer or easier.

heading: Brindlewick Robotics — Company Overview > How to use this handbook
text:
Brindlewick Robotics — Company Overview > How to use this handbook
This handbook covers policies for all permanent employees. Contractors should check their contract first. If something here conflicts with your employment contract, your contract wins. Questions about any policy go to the People Team in the #ask-people Slack channel.

heading: Expenses and Business Travel > Submitting expenses
text:
Expenses and Business Travel > Submitting expenses
Submit all expenses in **Ledgerline** within 30 days of spending the money. Expenses submitted later than 30 days need finance director approval and may be rejected.

Receipts are required for every expense over €25. Photos of receipts are accepted.

heading: Expenses and Business Travel > Approval limits
text:
Expenses and Business Travel > Approval limits
- Up to €500: approved automatically if within policy.
- Over €500: requires your manager's approval in Ledgerline **before** you spend the money.
- Over €5,000: requires approval from the finance director.

heading: Expenses and Business Travel > Flights
text:
Expenses and Business Travel > Flights
Book flights through the company travel tool, Skyroute. Economy class is standard for flights under 6 hours. For flights of 6 hours or more, premium economy is allowed. Business class is never reimbursed unless the CEO approves it in writing.

heading: Expenses and Business Travel > Hotels
text:
Expenses and Business Travel > Hotels
The hotel limit is €180 per night. In capital cities the limit is €240 per night. Bookings above the limit need manager approval.

heading: Expenses and Business Travel > Meals (per diem)
text:
Expenses and Business Travel > Meals (per diem)
When travelling for work, you may claim a daily meal allowance:

- Domestic travel: €55 per day
- International travel: €75 per day

Alcohol is not reimbursable, except at client dinners approved in advance by your manager.

heading: Expenses and Business Travel > Ground transport
text:
Expenses and Business Travel > Ground transport
Public transport or taxis are reimbursed. If you use your own car, mileage is reimbursed at €0.30 per kilometre. Parking fines and traffic fines are never reimbursed.

heading: IT and Security > Your equipment
text:
IT and Security > Your equipment
Every employee gets a company laptop. Engineers can choose between a 16-inch MacBook Pro and a Linux workstation laptop; everyone else receives a 14-inch MacBook Air. Laptops are replaced every 4 years.

You may not install unapproved software that handles company data. Ask in #it-help if you are unsure.

heading: IT and Security > Passwords and accounts
text:
IT and Security > Passwords and accounts
- Use the company password manager, **Vaultkey**, for all work passwords.
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory on every company account.
- Never share your password, even with IT. IT staff will never ask for it.

heading: IT and Security > VPN
text:
IT and Security > VPN
Connect to the company VPN, **Tunnelgate**, whenever you use public Wi-Fi (cafés, airports, hotels). The VPN is not required on your home network.

heading: IT and Security > Lost or stolen devices
text:
IT and Security > Lost or stolen devices
Report a lost or stolen laptop or phone within 2 hours by posting in #sec-alerts or calling the IT on-call number in Peoplepath. IT will wipe the device remotely. You will not be blamed for reporting quickly.

heading: IT and Security > Phishing
text:
IT and Security > Phishing
If you receive a suspicious email, do not click any links. Use the "Report phishing" button in your mail client. Every quarter, security runs a simulated phishing test; people who click receive a short refresher training, not a penalty.

heading: IT and Security > Data classification
text:
IT and Security > Data classification
All company information has one of four levels:

1. **Public** — can be shared with anyone (e.g. marketing pages).
2. **Internal** — for employees only (e.g. this handbook).
3. **Confidential** — limited to specific teams (e.g. customer contracts, salaries).
4. **Restricted** — highest sensitivity (e.g. Sorter-9 firmware signing keys). Access requires security team approval and is logged.

Confidential and Restricted data must never be pasted into external AI tools or personal cloud storage.

heading: Leave Policy > Annual leave
text:
Leave Policy > Annual leave
Full-time employees receive 27 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, plus public holidays in their country of employment. Part-time employees receive leave pro rata.

Request leave in the HR portal, Peoplepath, at least two weeks in advance for absences longer than three days.

### Carrying over leave

You may carry over up to 5 unused days into the next year. Carried-over days must be used by 31 March, or they are lost. Unused days beyond 5 are not paid out.

heading: Leave Policy > Recharge Week
text:
Leave Policy > Recharge Week
The whole company closes for **Recharge Week**, the last week of December. Recharge Week does not count against your 27 days. Field support runs a small on-call rota during this week; on-call staff receive the same number of days off in January.

heading: Leave Policy > Sick leave
text:
Leave Policy > Sick leave
If you are sick, tell your manager before 10:00 on the first day. You can self-certify sickness for up to 3 consecutive days. From the 4th consecutive day you need a doctor's note, uploaded to Peoplepath.

Sick leave is paid at full salary for up to 12 weeks in any rolling 12-month period.

heading: Leave Policy > Parental leave
text:
Leave Policy > Parental leave
- **Primary caregivers:** 20 weeks at full pay.
- **Secondary caregivers:** 8 weeks at full pay, to be taken within the first year after the birth or adoption.

Parental leave applies equally to birth, adoption and surrogacy. Notify the People Team at least 8 weeks before your planned start date.

heading: Leave Policy > Bereavement leave
text:
Leave Policy > Bereavement leave
Employees receive 5 days of paid bereavement leave for the loss of a close family member, and 2 days for other relatives or close friends. No documentation is required.

heading: Onboarding > Before your first day
text:
Onboarding > Before your first day
Your laptop and equipment are shipped to you 5 business days before your start date. You will receive your Peoplepath login by email the week before you start.

heading: Onboarding > Your first week
text:
Onboarding > Your first week
- **Day 1:** Welcome session with the People Team, laptop setup with IT, lunch with your team.
- **Day 2–3:** Security training (mandatory, about 2 hours) and product introduction to the Sorter-9.
- **Day 4–5:** Meet your onboarding buddy and start your first small task.

heading: Onboarding > Onboarding buddy
text:
Onboarding > Onboarding buddy
Every new hire is paired with an onboarding buddy from a different team. Your buddy is your go-to person for "how does this work here?" questions during your first 3 months.

heading: Onboarding > 30/60/90-day check-ins
text:
Onboarding > 30/60/90-day check-ins
Your manager holds structured check-ins at 30, 60 and 90 days. At each check-in you review your goals together and give feedback on the onboarding process.

heading: Onboarding > Probation
text:
Onboarding > Probation
The probation period is 6 months. During probation the notice period is 2 weeks for both sides. After probation, the standard notice period is 2 months. Your manager confirms the end of probation in writing.

heading: Onboarding > Visiting Kettering Bay
text:
Onboarding > Visiting Kettering Bay
All new employees, including software staff, spend one day at the Kettering Bay factory within their first 3 months to see the Sorter-9 being built and tested.

heading: Performance and Growth > Review cycles
text:
Performance and Growth > Review cycles
Brindlewick holds two performance reviews per year, in **April** and **October**. Each review includes a self-assessment, feedback from two peers of your choice, and a conversation with your manager.

heading: Performance and Growth > Ratings
text:
Performance and Growth > Ratings
Reviews use a three-level scale:

- **Exceeds** — consistently goes beyond the expectations of the role.
- **Meets** — fully delivers what the role requires.
- **Developing** — not yet meeting all expectations; a support plan is agreed.

heading: Performance and Growth > Promotions
text:
Performance and Growth > Promotions
Promotions are decided only in the October cycle. Your manager nominates you, and a promotion committee reviews the case. Promotions take effect on 1 January.

heading: Performance and Growth > Salary reviews
text:
Performance and Growth > Salary reviews
Salaries are reviewed once a year, also in the October cycle. Changes take effect on 1 January along with promotions.

heading: Performance and Growth > Internal transfers
text:
Performance and Growth > Internal transfers
After 12 months in your current role you may apply for open roles in other teams. You do not need your manager's permission to apply, but you should tell them before your final interview.

heading: Performance and Growth > Career levels
text:
Performance and Growth > Career levels
Each job family has levels from L1 (entry) to L6 (principal). Level descriptions are published in Peoplepath so you can see what is expected at the next level.

heading: Working Hours and Remote Work > Core hours
text:
Working Hours and Remote Work > Core hours
Brindlewick uses flexible hours. Everyone must be available during core hours, 10:00 to 15:00 local office time, Monday to Friday. Outside core hours you can arrange your day as you like, as long as you work your contracted hours (40 hours per week for full-time staff).

Kettering Bay manufacturing staff work fixed shifts instead of flexible hours. Shift schedules are published by the floor lead two weeks in advance.

heading: Working Hours and Remote Work > Hybrid work
text:
Working Hours and Remote Work > Hybrid work
Office-based employees work from the office at least two days per week. Tuesday and Thursday are **anchor days**, when teams meet in person. You may choose your other office days freely.

heading: Working Hours and Remote Work > Fully remote employees
text:
Working Hours and Remote Work > Fully remote employees
Fully remote employees must live in an approved country (currently: Netherlands, Portugal, Ireland, Poland and Germany). Remote employees travel to Port Halden for the twice-yearly **All-Hands Week**, and Brindlewick pays for that travel.

heading: Working Hours and Remote Work > Working from abroad
text:
Working Hours and Remote Work > Working from abroad
Any employee may work from another country for up to 30 days per calendar year. You need written approval from your manager and the People Team at least two weeks before you travel, because of tax and data-protection rules. Working from abroad for more than 30 days is not permitted.

heading: Working Hours and Remote Work > Home office setup
text:
Working Hours and Remote Work > Home office setup
New employees receive a one-time home office stipend of €400 for a chair, desk or monitor. Receipts must be submitted through Ledgerline within 60 days of your start date.
